lit: to make up a lot of feeling all by oneself

use.how: Predicate, often in 别自作多情了 or 是我自作多情. Mocks someone, or oneself, for reading affection or special attention into what was not meant that way.

near.diff: 一厢情愿 is any one-sided wish or plan the other side never agreed to; 自作多情 is wrongly believing someone has feelings for you.

cue: You thought the new colleague's smile and the coffee he brought meant he liked you, then learn he brings coffee for everyone.

ctx.s: 她只是对每个人都很客气，你别{自作多情}了。
ctx.en: She's just polite to everyone; don't kid yourself that she likes you.

ctx.s: 我还以为那束花是送给我的，原来是我{自作多情}。
ctx.en: I thought the flowers were for me; turns out I was flattering myself.

ctx.s: “他是不是喜欢我？”“人家只是借你的笔记，别{自作多情}。”
ctx.en: "Does he like me?" "He just borrowed your notes. Don't get ideas."

ctx.s: 他那条朋友圈根本不是写给你的，是你{自作多情}了。
ctx.en: That post of his wasn't written for you at all; you're reading too much into it.

ctx.s: 那天她冲我笑了一下，我就{自作多情}了好几个星期。
ctx.en: She smiled at me once that day, and I spent weeks imagining she was into me.

ctx.s: 说实话，我怕他对我好只是出于礼貌，是我{自作多情}，所以一直没敢表白。
ctx.en: Honestly, I was afraid he was only being kind out of politeness and I was imagining things, so I never dared to confess.

bad.s: 他对女朋友非常{自作多情}，每天都送礼物。
bad.en: (meant: he is very affectionate to his girlfriend)
bad.why: It does not mean affectionate; it means imagining feelings in someone else that are not there.

bad.s: 我们俩{自作多情}，下个月就结婚了。
bad.en: (meant: we are deeply in love and marrying next month)
bad.why: It mocks one-sided, imagined feelings, so it cannot describe a couple's mutual love.

lit: there is talking and there is laughing

use.how: Adverbial with 地 (有说有笑地走着) or predicate. Describes two or more people in relaxed, friendly conversation.

near.diff: 谈笑风生 is bookish and praises someone talking with wit and ease; 有说有笑 is everyday and just says people are chatting cheerfully.

cue: On the bus home after a school trip, the students chat and laugh the whole way. How were they travelling?

ctx.s: 下课后，同学们{有说有笑}地走出教室。
ctx.en: After class, the students walked out of the classroom chatting and laughing.

ctx.s: 一家人围着桌子吃饭，{有说有笑}，特别热闹。
ctx.en: The whole family sat round the table eating, talking and laughing; it was very lively.

ctx.s: 刚才你们俩还{有说有笑}的，怎么突然吵起来了？
ctx.en: A moment ago you two were chatting and laughing; how come you're suddenly arguing?

ctx.s: 他们一路上{有说有笑}，一点儿也不觉得累。
ctx.en: They talked and laughed all the way and didn't feel tired at all.

ctx.s: 看到她和新同事{有说有笑}，我就放心了。
ctx.en: Seeing her chatting and laughing with her new colleagues, I stopped worrying.

ctx.s: 以前他总是一个人待着，现在也能跟大家{有说有笑}了。
ctx.en: He used to keep to himself, but now he chats and jokes with everyone.

bad.s: 这个笑话很{有说有笑}，大家都笑了。
bad.en: (meant: the joke was very funny)
bad.why: It describes people chatting and laughing together, not how funny a joke or a thing is.

bad.s: 考试的时候，教室里{有说有笑}，非常安静。
bad.en: (meant: during the exam the room was very quiet)
bad.why: It means people are talking and laughing, the opposite of a silent exam room.

mean: full of praise, unable to stop praising

use.how: Predicate whose subject is the people praising: 大家对这道菜赞不绝口, 让人赞不绝口. Not used with 很 or 非常.

near.diff: 交口称赞 stresses that many people praise with one voice; 赞不绝口 stresses that the praise keeps coming.

cue: Every guest at dinner keeps telling the host how wonderful the fish is, again and again, all evening.

ctx.s: 客人们吃了妈妈包的饺子，个个{赞不绝口}。
ctx.en: The guests tried Mum's dumplings and every one of them couldn't stop praising them.

ctx.s: 老师对他的作文{赞不绝口}，还在班上念了一遍。
ctx.en: The teacher was full of praise for his essay and even read it out to the class.

ctx.s: 去过那家民宿的朋友都{赞不绝口}，我们也订了一间。
ctx.en: Friends who've stayed at that guesthouse rave about it, so we booked a room too.

ctx.s: “那部电影怎么样？”“我爸看完{赞不绝口}，说是今年最好看的。”
ctx.en: "How's that film?" "My dad couldn't stop praising it; he says it's the best this year."

ctx.s: 新同事做的方案让经理{赞不绝口}。
ctx.en: The new colleague's proposal had the manager singing its praises.

ctx.s: 这位老师傅的手艺，连行家都{赞不绝口}。
ctx.en: Even experts can't stop praising this old master's craftsmanship.

bad.s: 这道菜非常{赞不绝口}。
bad.en: (meant: this dish is excellent)
bad.why: It describes the people doing the praising, not the thing praised, and it cannot take 'very' before it.

bad.s: 他的报告错误太多，经理看了{赞不绝口}。
bad.en: (meant: the manager kept complaining about it)
bad.why: It means non-stop praise, so it cannot describe non-stop criticism of a bad report.

use.how: Mostly an attribute (激动人心的时刻, 激动人心的消息) or predicate. Said of events, moments, news or speeches, never of one's own feeling.

near.diff: 惊心动魄 is thrilling because of danger or tension that grips you; 激动人心 is thrilling because it is exciting and uplifting.
振奋人心 stresses boosting morale and confidence; 激动人心 stresses excitement in the moment.

cue: The countdown hits zero, the rocket lifts off, and the whole crowd jumps to its feet cheering. What kind of moment is it?

ctx.s: 宣布我们队夺冠的那一刻，是全场最{激动人心}的时刻。
ctx.en: The announcement that our team had won the title was the most thrilling moment of the whole event.

ctx.s: 好了，下面就是{激动人心}的抽奖环节！
ctx.en: Right, now for the exciting part: the prize draw!

ctx.s: 第一次亲眼看到火箭发射，真是{激动人心}。
ctx.en: Seeing a rocket launch with my own eyes for the first time was truly thrilling.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼上，校长发表了一篇{激动人心}的演讲。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony, the principal gave a stirring speech.

ctx.s: 站上领奖台、听到国歌响起，难道不是很{激动人心}吗？
ctx.en: Standing on the podium and hearing the anthem play: isn't that thrilling?

ctx.s: 孩子们盼了一年的春游终于到了，这对他们来说是{激动人心}的一天。
ctx.en: The spring outing the children had looked forward to all year finally came; for them it was a thrilling day.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，我非常{激动人心}。
bad.en: (meant: I was very excited to hear the good news)
bad.why: It describes what stirs people, not the speaker's own feeling; for that, plain 'excited' (jidong) is used.

bad.s: 医生说他的病加重了，真是一个{激动人心}的消息。
bad.en: (meant: this is shocking, upsetting news)
bad.why: It is positive and uplifting; it cannot describe bad or frightening news.

mean: bullying the weak and fearing the strong
lit: bully the soft, fear the hard

use.how: Predicate or attribute (欺软怕硬的人). Condemns someone who pushes the weak around but gives in to anyone strong.

near.diff: 仗势欺人 is bullying others by leaning on one's power or connections; 欺软怕硬 stresses the double standard: harsh to the weak, meek to the strong.

cue: A man shouts at the waiter and the cleaner but turns polite and meek the moment the manager appears.

ctx.s: 那只大狗{欺软怕硬}，只敢冲小狗叫。
ctx.en: That big dog is a bully and a coward; it only dares to bark at small dogs.

ctx.s: “为什么他只对你发脾气？”“因为他{欺软怕硬}啊。”
ctx.en: "Why does he only lose his temper with you?" "Because he picks on the weak and backs down to the strong."

ctx.s: 你别怕他，这种人{欺软怕硬}，你一强硬他就退了。
ctx.en: Don't be afraid of him; his type bullies the weak, and the moment you stand firm he backs off.

ctx.s: 他对新人大呼小叫，见了经理却一声不吭，真是{欺软怕硬}。
ctx.en: He yells at the new staff but doesn't say a word in front of the manager; a classic bully.

ctx.s: 小时候班上有个{欺软怕硬}的男生，专挑个子小的同学欺负。
ctx.en: When I was little there was a boy in my class who picked on the weak and only ever bullied the small kids.

ctx.s: 有的商家{欺软怕硬}，老实人投诉没人理，会闹的马上退款。
ctx.en: Some shops bully the meek: quiet customers' complaints get ignored, while those who kick up a fuss get refunds at once.

bad.s: 他{欺软怕硬}，所以从来不跟人吵架。
bad.en: (meant: he is timid and avoids conflict)
bad.why: It is not mere timidity; it means bullying the weak while giving in to the strong.

bad.s: 这位警察{欺软怕硬}，总是保护弱者。
bad.en: (meant: he stands up to the strong to protect the weak)
bad.why: That is the opposite: the idiom condemns someone who bullies the weak, not one who protects them.

lit: yin and yang, a strange air: an odd, ambiguous manner

use.how: Adverbial (阴阳怪气地说), predicate or complement (说话阴阳怪气的). Describes a veiled, insinuating tone that says one thing and means a jab.

near.diff: 冷嘲热讽 is open mockery and ridicule; 阴阳怪气 is an indirect, insinuating tone where the jab is hidden.

cue: Hearing you got the promotion, a coworker smirks: 'Oh, congratulations, boss, we're all so lucky to have you.' How is he talking?

ctx.s: 有话直说，别{阴阳怪气}的。
ctx.en: If you've got something to say, say it straight; stop being snide.

ctx.s: 她最近说话总是{阴阳怪气}的，是不是对我有意见？
ctx.en: She's been so snide with me lately; does she have a problem with me?

ctx.s: 他一听我升职了，就{阴阳怪气}地说：“哟，以后得叫你领导了。”
ctx.en: As soon as he heard about my promotion, he sneered: "Oh, I suppose I'll have to call you boss now."

ctx.s: 我只是晚到了五分钟，你用不着这么{阴阳怪气}吧？
ctx.en: I was only five minutes late; there's no need to be so sarcastic, is there?

ctx.s: 网上有些评论{阴阳怪气}，看了让人很不舒服。
ctx.en: Some online comments are so snide they make you feel uncomfortable reading them.

ctx.s: 她嘴上说“你真厉害”，可那{阴阳怪气}的语气谁都听得出来。
ctx.en: She said "Aren't you clever", but everyone could hear the sarcasm in her voice.

bad.s: 他讲笑话很{阴阳怪气}，大家都笑得很开心。
bad.en: (meant: he tells jokes in a quirky, funny way)
bad.why: It criticises a snide, insinuating tone; it is not praise for quirky humour.

bad.s: 他气坏了，{阴阳怪气}地大骂了我一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he was furious and shouted at me)
bad.why: It describes veiled, indirect sarcasm, not open, angry shouting.

mean: in total uproar (a household in chaos)
lit: the chickens fly up and the dogs leap about

use.how: Predicate or complement after 得 (闹得鸡飞狗跳, 忙得鸡飞狗跳). Said of a home or group thrown into noisy commotion, often wryly.

near.diff: 鸡犬不宁 stresses that someone's harassment gives everyone no peace; 鸡飞狗跳 paints the noisy scene of everyone rushing about.
乱七八糟 is a messy state of things; 鸡飞狗跳 is a commotion of people in motion.

cue: The alarm didn't go off, the kids can't find their shoes, the dog is barking and everyone is running around shouting.

ctx.s: 两个孩子一闹，家里就{鸡飞狗跳}的。
ctx.en: Once the two kids start acting up, the house is in total uproar.

ctx.s: 早上全家都起晚了，忙得{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: The whole family overslept this morning, and it was utter chaos.

ctx.s: “你家猫又干什么了？”“它打翻了鱼缸，家里一下子{鸡飞狗跳}。”
ctx.en: "What has your cat done now?" "It knocked over the fish tank and the whole house went into uproar."

ctx.s: 装修那个月，我们家天天{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: The month we were renovating, our home was in chaos every day.

ctx.s: 过年时亲戚们进进出出，屋里{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: At New Year, relatives were coming and going, and the house was in uproar.

ctx.s: 新经理一来就改了所有规定，整个部门被搞得{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: The new manager changed every rule the moment he arrived, and the whole department was thrown into chaos.

bad.s: 他的书桌上{鸡飞狗跳}，到处都是纸。
bad.en: (meant: his desk is a mess, with papers everywhere)
bad.why: It describes a noisy commotion of people rushing about, not a still mess of objects; for a messy desk use luan qi ba zao.

bad.s: 音乐会结束时，观众{鸡飞狗跳}，热烈鼓掌。
bad.en: (meant: the audience applauded enthusiastically)
bad.why: It means chaos and disorder, not enthusiasm or warm applause.

lit: chicken feathers and garlic skins: worthless scraps

use.how: Mostly an attribute: 鸡毛蒜皮的小事, 鸡毛蒜皮的矛盾. Dismisses everyday matters as too trivial to matter.

near.diff: 小题大做 is the act of making a big fuss over a small matter; 鸡毛蒜皮 names the small matter itself.

cue: A couple argues for an hour over who forgot to buy toilet paper. What kind of matter are they fighting about?

ctx.s: 为了这点{鸡毛蒜皮}的小事，你们俩至于吵架吗？
ctx.en: Is it really worth you two fighting over such a petty little thing?

ctx.s: 他每天回家都跟我说办公室里那些{鸡毛蒜皮}的事。
ctx.en: Every day he comes home and tells me about all the petty goings-on at the office.

ctx.s: 邻居之间难免有些{鸡毛蒜皮}的矛盾，互相让一让就好了。
ctx.en: Neighbours are bound to have petty squabbles; just give a little on both sides.

ctx.s: 社区工作很琐碎，处理的大多是{鸡毛蒜皮}的事情。
ctx.en: Community work is fiddly; most of what you deal with is trivial stuff.

ctx.s: 别拿这些{鸡毛蒜皮}的事去烦老板，你自己处理就行。
ctx.en: Don't bother the boss with these trivial things; just handle them yourself.

ctx.s: 伤感情的往往不是大事，而是一件件{鸡毛蒜皮}的小事。
ctx.en: What hurts a relationship is often not the big things but one petty little thing after another.

bad.s: 这次地震造成了很多{鸡毛蒜皮}的损失。
bad.en: (meant: the earthquake caused many small losses)
bad.why: It dismisses petty everyday matters; it cannot describe real damage, let alone from a disaster.

bad.s: 她做事很{鸡毛蒜皮}，每个细节都检查。
bad.en: (meant: she is meticulous and checks every detail)
bad.why: It describes trivial matters, not a careful, meticulous person.

lit: not even a crow or a sparrow makes a sound

use.how: Predicate of a place or crowd: 教室里鸦雀无声, often with 顿时 or 一下子. Describes a group of people who are, or suddenly fall, completely silent.

near.diff: 夜深人静 is the quiet of late night when everyone is asleep; 鸦雀无声 is a roomful of people making no sound.

cue: The teacher slams a book on the desk, and the noisy class of forty instantly stops talking. Not a sound.

ctx.s: 老师一走进来，教室里马上{鸦雀无声}。
ctx.en: The moment the teacher walked in, the classroom went dead quiet.

ctx.s: 刚才还吵吵闹闹的，怎么一下子{鸦雀无声}了？
ctx.en: It was so noisy a second ago; why has everyone suddenly gone silent?

ctx.s: 考场里{鸦雀无声}，只听见笔在纸上写字的声音。
ctx.en: The exam hall was utterly silent except for the scratching of pens on paper.

ctx.s: 电影放到最后一幕，整个电影院{鸦雀无声}。
ctx.en: When the film reached its final scene, the whole cinema was completely silent.

ctx.s: 他说完那句话，会议室里顿时{鸦雀无声}，谁也不敢接话。
ctx.en: When he finished saying that, the meeting room fell silent and nobody dared respond.

ctx.s: 校长问是谁打碎了窗户，台下{鸦雀无声}。
ctx.en: The principal asked who had broken the window, and the assembly was utterly silent.

bad.s: 我的手机一整天{鸦雀无声}，一个电话也没有。
bad.en: (meant: my phone was silent all day, no calls)
bad.why: It describes a place or crowd of people being silent, not a phone with no calls.

bad.s: 他{鸦雀无声}地看着我，什么都没说。
bad.en: (meant: he looked at me without a word)
bad.why: It is said of a place full of people, not of one person keeping quiet; for that say yi sheng bu keng.

mean: the slow must start early (often said modestly)
lit: the clumsy bird takes off first

use.how: A clause on its own, often 笨鸟先飞嘛 or 我是笨鸟先飞. Usually said modestly of oneself to explain starting early or working extra.

near.diff: 勤能补拙 is a general maxim that hard work makes up for lack of talent; 笨鸟先飞 is about starting earlier than others.

cue: Knowing you're slower than your classmates, you begin revising a month before anyone else. How do you modestly explain it?

ctx.s: “你怎么这么早就开始复习了？”“{笨鸟先飞}嘛，我基础差。”
ctx.en: "Why have you started revising so early?" "The slow bird has to set off first; my basics are weak."

ctx.s: 我学得慢，只好{笨鸟先飞}，每天早到一个小时练习。
ctx.en: I'm a slow learner, so I have to make up for it by coming in an hour early to practise.

ctx.s: 我知道自己不如别人聪明，所以{笨鸟先飞}，暑假就开始预习了。
ctx.en: I know I'm not as bright as the others, so I got a head start and began preparing in the summer holidays.

ctx.s: 他总说自己是{笨鸟先飞}，其实他是我们组最能干的。
ctx.en: He always says he just starts early to make up for being slow, but he's actually the most capable in our group.

ctx.s: 刚进公司那年，她{笨鸟先飞}，每天最早一个到办公室。
ctx.en: Her first year at the company, she made up for inexperience by being first into the office every day.

ctx.s: 学外语没有捷径，{笨鸟先飞}，早点开始总没错。
ctx.en: There are no shortcuts in learning a language; if you're slow, start early, and you can't go wrong.

bad.s: 他总是拖到最后一天才开始写作业，真是{笨鸟先飞}。
bad.en: (meant: he always leaves his homework to the last minute)
bad.why: It means starting early to make up for being slow; it cannot describe putting things off until the last minute.

bad.s: 他最聪明，所以{笨鸟先飞}，第一个交了卷。
bad.en: (meant: he is the smartest, so he finished first)
bad.why: It means starting early to make up for being slow, not finishing first because of talent.
